title: snapshot-driven RAG linter + local telemetry probe for quickstarts
author: Priya N. Kapoor
release_notes: Add snapshot-driven RAG linter and local telemetry probes to quickstarts; improved authoring feedback and CI snapshot checks.
description:
Motivation: When iterating on RAG prompt templates and tool-call bindings, subtle output regressions can slip past unit tests. This PR adds a snapshot-driven linter and a small local telemetry probe so authors can catch semantic drift in quickstarts before pushing changes.

What this PR does (single-line summary): Introduce a CLI-backed 'snaplint' tool for quickstarts, snapshot assertion schema for RAG sessions, lightweight local telemetry probes for developer feedback, and docs/quickstart updates to demonstrate usage.

Details: The snaplint tool records synthetic RAG session traces (prompt, retrieved snippets, model output, tool calls) into a normalized snapshot format and validates them against user-provided assertions (string containment, jsonpath, token-count ranges, structured-output schema). It supports a watch mode for live authoring and a --update-snapshots flag for intentional updates. The telemetry probe runs alongside the quickstart runner and emits compact dev-metrics (prefix latency percentiles, retrieval hit rate, model-confusion warnings) to STDOUT and an optional local SQLite store for offline inspection.

Why this belongs in quickstarts/docs: The goal is to give developers a low-friction feedback loop so template authors and examples maintain behavioral guarantees over time. This is intentionally lightweight (no external services) so it can be included in local dev workflows and CI smoke checks.

Checklist (what I changed):
- [x] CLI snaplint tool (snaplint.js) with snapshot format v1 and assertion support
- [x] Local telemetry probe (telemetry_probe.py) for quickstarts with stdout emitter and optional sqlite storage
- [x] Example snapshot and assertions for the 'local-rag-authoring' quickstart
- [x] Docs quickstart guide: docs/quickstarts/snaplint.md with examples and troubleshooting
- [x] Unit tests + small e2e smoke runner integrated into existing quickstart test harness
- [x] CI job added to run snaplint checks on quickstart snapshots
- [x] Authoring watch-mode integration to show assertion failures inline in the author console

Review thread (summary of conversation):
- Maya Chen (reviewer): "Nice UX. Can we keep snapshot format strictly stable? I suggest adding a version header and a deterministic serializer to avoid spurious diffs."
  - Author (Priya): "Agreed. Added explicit \"format_version\": \"v1\" field and a serializer that sorts injected metadata, see tools/snaplint/serializer.js commit."
- Lucas Rivera (reviewer): "Telemetry probe is handy but I'd prefer it not require Python deps during standard quickstart runs. Can telemetry probe fall back to pure-stdout mode?"
  - Author: "Yes — the probe defaults to pure-stdout and only imports sqlite3 when --db-path is provided. Updated docs to call this out."
- Gina Park (reviewer): "CI flake: e2e failed in first run due to a race in the test harness capturing stdout; could you make the smoke runner retry?"
  - Author: "Added a small retry wrapper in tests/snaplint/smoke_runner.py: 3 attempts with exponential backoff. Reran CI locally before pushing."
- Lucas: "LGTM after tiny lint fix (consistent CLI exit codes)."
- Maya: "Approved."

CI summary and timeline: 
- Initial CI run (2026-02-16): unit tests - pass; lint - pass; e2e smoke - fail (race on stdout capture).
- Fix pushed (2026-02-17): added retry wrapper and deterministic serializer; re-trigger CI.
- Second CI run (2026-02-18): unit tests - pass; lint - pass; e2e smoke - pass.
- Final CI run (2026-02-19): all checks green; maintainers approved and merged.

How to try locally (short):
1) cd quickstarts/local-rag-authoring
2) npm install (for snaplint CLI) or use npx to run snaplint.js
3) python3 tools/telemetry/telemetry_probe.py --watch --db-path ./snaptelemetry.db (optional)
4) ./tools/snaplint/snaplint.js validate --snapshot snapshots/example-1.snap.json --assertions snapshots/example-1.assert.json

Backward compatibility and migration notes: Snapshots include a format_version field; current default is v1 and CI checks will only run if snapshots contain that field. Future format changes should introduce v2 and include migration guidance in docs/quickstarts/snaplint.md.

Security considerations: Telemetry probe only writes to a local sqlite file by default; no network access. Snapshots should be sanitized before committing (be careful not to include PII). The docs include a small checklist for sanitization.

Merge outcome: Squash merged to main on 2026-02-20 by Maya Chen. Merge commit message: "Add snaplint (snapshot-driven RAG linter) and local telemetry probe; docs and CI smoke job. (ENG-1198)"

Notes for maintainers: If we want this as an opt-in global CI job, we should gate the workflow on a repo-level flag. For now the job is in the quickstarts workflow directory and runs only when quickstart files change.
